content.overview: BNS s. 204 — Personating a public servant.
content.study:
Introduction and meaning
Personating a public servant. BNS restatement of IPC 170. Elements are substantially the same; cite the BNS number for offences on or after 1 July 2024. BNS restatement of IPC 170. Cite the BNS number for facts on or after 1 July 2024.
In student language: BNS s. 204 is the rule on “Personating a public servant”. The section provides that whoever pretends to hold any particular office as a public servant, knowing that he does not hold such office or falsely personates any other person holding such office, and in such assumed character does or attempts to do any act under colour of such office, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which shall not be less than six months but which may extend to three years and with fine. Do not stop at the heading. An examiner awards marks for the ingredients, the explanations and the illustrations, not for writing the title alone.

Why this is asked
Criminal law arguments turn on statutory ingredients. BNS s. 204 exists so that “Personating a public servant” has a closed legal test in Chapter XII — Of Offences by or Relating to Public Servants. An authoritative analysis defines the concept, lists every ingredient, walks the statutory illustrations, states exceptions, and applies the test methodically to facts.
Chapter setting: Disobedience, unlawful trade, personation — and a new duty to treat a victim.

hypotheticals.question: Whether BNS s. 204 (Personating a public servant) applies, and how structured written arguments should be framed.
hypotheticals.analysis:
Step 1 — Identify the provision. The correct current-law cite is BNS s. 204 (Personating a public servant), Chapter XII — Of Offences by or Relating to Public Servants.
Step 2 — State the legal test in your own words, then list the ingredients:
   (1) Whoever pretends to hold any particular office as a public servant, knowing that he does not hold such office or falsely personates any other person holding such office, and in such assumed character does or attempts to do any act under colour of such office, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which shall not be less than six months but which may extend to three years and with fine
Step 3 — Check limitations, provisos and the rest of the Chapter so you do not apply s. 204 in a vacuum.
Step 4 — Map each fact to an ingredient. Write “this fact proves ingredient (a)” or “this fact is missing, so the section is not made out”.
Step 5 — Conclude. If every essential ingredient is proved and no exception covers the case, BNS s. 204 applies. If any essential ingredient fails, say so and stop. Do not invent a different section to save the answer.
